title: Every Time I Feel the Spirit
description: The spiritual as Hampton Institute sang it, for 2 to 4 singers: everyone sings the refrain in harmony, twice, and the alto sings each verse alone. The refrain, two verses, and the refrain after each, at an easy walking pace.

credits.words: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (printed 1909)
credits.tune: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (printed 1909)

licence.words: public domain: traditional, printed 1909 by Hampton Institute
licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella; the printed four-part refrain (1909, "arranged by the musical directors", and Dett's 1927 edition) was used only to check the chords. Accepted exceptions (singable.py): the verses are the tune's own solo line as printed (1909), sung by the alto as the licence says: each line falls a fifth from G to C and climbs back by the printed arpeggio C, E flat, G, not by step ("my Lord", "Out His", "All a-", "looks so", "Ask my"); and where the tune falls to its lowest note, E flat, on "pray." (six times) the alto sings G, a third above it, so the duet keeps the chord's third.
licence.source: tune and words from Religious Folk Songs of the Negro as Sung on the Plantations, New Edition, "arranged by the musical directors of the Hampton Normal and Agricultural Institute", "from the original edition by Thomas P. Fenner" (Hampton, Va.: The Institute Press, 1909), which names no other editor or arranger (Fenner died 1912; the musical directors are unnamed, and Robert R. Moton signs only its note to the new edition), p. 169, archive.org/details/religiousfolkson00hamp (leaf n178); in E-flat in 4/4, every pitch and rhythm as printed; the tempo ours (Dett's 1927 reprint of the same setting, p. 169, marks crotchet = 68 to 72; Dett died 1943; consulted only); the refrain (sung twice, as its repeat marks say), then verses 1 and 2 of the three printed, each followed by the refrain twice (D.C.); the solo verse is sung by the alto; breaths written in for beginners; the verse words are printed as a block under the solo line, so their fitting to its notes is ours
